extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and examiners interacting with the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing and filing patent application documents (cover sheet, specification, drawings, abstract) and for meeting the enablement/description requirements before the Korean Intellectual Property Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application cover sheet required contents (Article 42(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application cover sheet must state: 1) the name and domicile of the patent applicant (if a corporation, its name and place of business); 2) the name and domicile or place of business of an agent if represented (if a patent firm, its name/place of business and the name of the designated patent attorney); 3) the title of the invention; 4) the name and domicile of the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover sheet shall be accompanied by a specification, necessary drawings, and an abstract. The cover sheet should also indicate applicant code, priority claim, claim on grace period disclosure exception and request for examination. The title on the cover sheet must be identical to that in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract usage and limits (Article 42(2) / Article 43)
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is to be used only for technical information and shall not be used to define the scope of the invention for which patent protection is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts facilitate searching and disclosure but cannot determine claim scope (Article 97). Matters disclosed only in an abstract do not constitute content of another application (Article 29(3)) and cannot be added to the specification by amendment. If an abstract is missing or deficient, the applicant will be requested to amend; continued deficiency may lead to invalidation of the application proceeding. Examiners should not cite Article 42(3) or (4) as grounds for rejection merely because an abstract is incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must contain description and claims (Article 42(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A specification filed at the time of filing must contain the description of the invention and the claims; necessary drawings and an abstract should accompany it. Claims may be omitted at filing but must be submitted by the period specified under Article 42-2(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification serves both as the right-document (defines scope) and as a technical disclosure. Guidelines on preparing description and claims are set out in Chapters 3 and 4. The description must enable the invention and satisfy method/format rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the invention: brevity, content and identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention shall be written briefly and concisely according to the subject matter of the invention and shall be identical in the cover sheet and the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ambiguous or wordy titles (examples given). Do not include a person's name, trademark, product nickname, expressions indicating only abstract functions, or the word 'patent' (examples: 'Upgraded', 'Improved'). If claims cover multiple categories (product, process, device, use), use a concise encompassing title (example: 'Paper, manufacturing process and manufacturing device thereof'). The title should clearly indicate what is claimed (example guidance for automatic control device vs automatic temperature control device). If claims change by amendment, amend the title accordingly. If title is inappropriate, examiner will notify and may suggest a proper title; inappropriate title alone is not a ground for rejection, though an examiner may ex officio amend titles when granting a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: In the section for the brief description of drawing(s), state what each drawing displays (e.g., 'Drawing 1 is the ground view of the whole assembly').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the brief description of drawings is inappropriate, it will be handled similarly to an inappropriate title (examiner notification, suggestion, possible order for amendment). Examples of brief description phrasing are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: when required and preparation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings may be attached when necessary for explanation of the claimed invention and shall be prepared according to the guideline for drawings of Annexed Form No.17 of the Enforcement Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where drawings are difficult to prepare per Annexed Form No.17 (e.g., crystal structures, particle shapes, oscilloscope results) or pictures better describe an embodiment, pictures may replace drawings. Pictures must be clear enough for publication in the official gazette; grayscale or color may be accepted if unavoidable. Utility model registration applications must include drawings; absence leads to illegitimate application returned to applicant. Irrelevant drawings (e.g., drawings from another application) that give rise to a ground for rejection under Article 42(3)(i) must be noted by the examiner; if the drawing error does not affect practice of the invention it may be treated as reference only. Submitting new drawings as amendment can constitute addition of new matter—examiners must be cautious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement / clarity and detail requirement (Article 42(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall describe the invention with such clarity and in such detail that a person skilled in the art can easily practice the invention based on ordinary skill, the specification and drawings at the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'A person skilled in the art' is defined as a technician with average understanding in the technical field. 'Easily practicing' means the skilled person fully understands and can reproduce the invention without adding special knowledge, undue trial and error, or repetitive experimentation. The invention to be enabled is the invention as recited in the claims; material disclosed only in the description but not in claims is not judged under Article 42(3)(i) for enablement of the claimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement for product inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claims recite a product invention, the description must enable a person skilled in the art to produce and use the product; generally the manufacturing method needs to be fully described unless the product can be manufactured based on the specification and drawings and the ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclosure should allow the product to be fully grasped from the whole disclosure and describe the roles and functions of special technical features. For use of the product, meaningful and specific uses should be described in technical terms unless the use is obvious from the spec/drawings at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement for method (process) inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims recite a method invention, the description must contain clear and full explanation so a skilled person is enabled to use the method; the roles and sequences of each step specifying the process should be described together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full disclosure of the steps and their sequences is expected so that the method can be practiced without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement for manufacturing method inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For manufacturing method claims, the description must enable a skilled person to produce a product by the claimed manufacturing method; the manufacturing method itself and roles/sequences of each step must be fully described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A manufacturing method generally consists of detailed steps dealing with raw materials—raw materials and a series of detailed steps must be fully described. The product manufactured by the method should be clearly described, except where the product is easily understood from raw materials or steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical substance inventions: experimental disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For chemical substance inventions, the name or chemical formula alone is usually not enabling. Detailed manufacturing methods, reaction conditions and direct experimental confirmation must be described unless the skilled person would easily understand the reaction at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embodiments should include detailed reaction conditions necessary for manufacturing (starting materials, temperature, pressure, inflow/outflow) and the results of direct experiments under such conditions. Low predictability/reproducibility means experimental data is often necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicinal (use) inventions: demonstration of effect
rubrics_metrics.description: For chemical/medicinal use inventions, the effect of the invention should be disclosed in the description; medicinal inventions require medical data proving effect or a sufficiently detailed description replacing such data, except where the medical mechanism is clearly known at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because predictability/reproducibility may be low, experimental/clinical data are usually necessary to support that the medicine has the claimed medical effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter inventions: required disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions including proprietary parameters, the technical content of the parameter must be described so a skilled person can realize the invention; detailed disclosure must include definition/technical meaning, numerical scope and reason for limits, method/conditions/devices for measuring the parameter, manufacturing method to meet the parameter, embodiments that fulfill the parameter, comparative examples that do not, and explanation of relation between parameter and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the detailed technical content is not explicitly stated but is clearly understandable considering the level of skill at filing, the examiner shall not decide lack of enablement. The disclosure must allow realization of the parameter-based invention without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of claims by description; genus/species and Markush issues (Article 42(4)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be supported by the description such that the subject matter of the claims is disclosed in the description. If claims cover a generic invention (genus) but the description only discloses species embodiments and the genus cannot be clearly recognized, Article 42(4)(i) applies. Conversely, if claims recite species but the description discloses only the genus and the species is not clearly recognized, Article 42(4)(i) applies. Article 42(3) may apply when other embodiments within the claimed genus cannot be easily practiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) Extrusion molding claims broadly covering many materials but description only details edible plastics—examiner should notify rejection under Article 42(3) or 42(4)(i) as appropriate. (2) Claims reciting broad oxygen-absorbing compositions with precise numeric constituents while description only discloses a narrower embodiment—examiner should notify lack of support. Markush groups: if only some group members have embodiments and others lack embodiments enabling practice, examiner shall notify rejection under Article 42(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term consistency between description and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If terms used in the description and the claims do not clearly match, an examiner shall notify a ground for rejection citing violation of Article 42(4)(i) since the invention recited in the claims is deemed not supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistent terminology between claims and specification; inconsistent terms can lead to rejection for lack of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description method requirements / arrangement of sections (Article 21 Enforcement Rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description of the invention shall include the following sections (in principle): title of the invention; technical field; background art; prior art literature; summary of the invention (including technical task, solution means, effects); brief description of drawings; detailed description for practicing the invention; industrial applicability; consignment number; sequence listing free text; and other necessary matters so a person skilled in the art can understand and reproduce the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sections need not be separately prepared if their contents are understood from the overall description. Sections that cannot be filled out for certain inventions may be omitted (example: chance discovery of a new substance may omit technical objectives if the substance/method is well understood from the description). The purpose is to clarify the technical matters and advance disclosed and to enable examiners/third parties to understand what technical tasks are solved and by what means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination process for enablement and support (basic considerations and special cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners assess enablement and support by considering the type of invention (product, method, manufacturing method) and special cases (chemical, medicinal, parameter inventions). Lack of sufficient manufacturing steps, experimental data, or disclosure for all claimed embodiments can lead to notices of rejection under Article 42(3) or 42(4)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners shall apply the criteria consistently to maintain examination efficiency. Examples and illustrations indicate how to apply Article 42(3) vs 42(4)(i) depending on whether the description lacks enablement or lacks support for the claimed scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for applications filed by KIPO-affiliated organization employees
rubrics_metrics.description: If an employee of a KIPO-affiliated organization (e.g., a prior art search institution) files a patent application while working for the institution, the examiner shall request a search from an outside prior art search institution and perform examination accordingly. If grantable, three examiners consult and then decide on allowance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a conflict/independence safeguard to ensure impartial prior art search and examination when an affiliated organization employee files the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to obtain a patent cannot be pledged prior to registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The entitlement to obtain a patent shall not be the subject of a pledge; where a pledge is established upon the entitlement to obtain a patent (i.e., before title/registration), the pledge shall not be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Once a patent right or utility model right is registered, a pledge can be established upon the registered right (e.g., patent right) according to the note.
